Let
\[
h(u,t)=20t^6+60t^5+180t^4+120t^3+180t^2
+210ut^4+600ut^3+900ut^2+360ut+180u
+180u^2t^2+240u^2t+180u^2+20u^3+20.
\]

Define \((u_0,t_0)\) to be the unique real solution in
\[
1.21087<u<1.21089,\qquad 1.14608<t<1.14609
\]
of
\[
\begin{aligned}
0={}&-4u^2(t+1)^2-u(2t^4+24t^3+36t^2+8t)\\
&\qquad +5t^6+14t^5+19t^4+20t^3+18t^2+12t+4,\\
0={}&4u^3(t+1)+u^2(2t^3+10t^2+18t+10)\\
&\qquad +u(-5t^5-25t^4-34t^3+6t^2+18t+6)\\
&\qquad -t^6-4t^5-t^4+6t^2+4t .
\end{aligned}
\]

Then
\[
A=\frac1{\sqrt{2(1+u_0+t_0^2)}},\qquad
B=A\sqrt{u_0},\qquad
C=At_0,
\]
and
\[
M_*=\frac{h(u_0,t_0)}{8(1+u_0+t_0^2)^3}.
\]

Numerically,
\[
(A,B,C)\approx(0.376654488472952,\ 0.414470409489182,\ 0.431677745512841),
\]
and
\[
M_*\approx 16.1110789070140.
\]

Thus the exact maximizing set is
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal E_*=
\{(\varepsilon A,\varepsilon\delta B,\varepsilon C):\varepsilon,\delta\in\{\pm1\}\}
}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\bigl(M_*,\mathcal E_*\bigr)
=
\left(
\frac{h(u_0,t_0)}{8(1+u_0+t_0^2)^3},
\{(\varepsilon A,\varepsilon\delta B,\varepsilon C):\varepsilon,\delta=\pm1\}
\right).
}
\]

The reduction is as follows. Writing
\[
f_{a,b,c}(\theta)=2e^{3i\theta}
\bigl(a\cos3\theta+b\cos2\theta+c\cos\theta\bigr),
\]
the normalization is
\[
a^2+b^2+c^2=\frac12.
\]
The sixth moment is the homogeneous polynomial
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(a,b,c)={}&20a^6+20b^6+20c^6+180a^4b^2+180a^4c^2+180a^2b^4\\
&+900a^2b^2c^2+180a^2c^4+180b^4c^2+210b^2c^4\\
&+120a^3c^3+360a^3b^2c+60ac^5+600ab^2c^3+240ab^4c.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(a\ne0\), put \(u=(b/a)^2\), \(t=c/a\). Then
\[
P=\frac{h(u,t)}{8(1+u+t^2)^3}.
\]
The displayed two polynomial equations are exactly the stationary equations in \(u,t\).

A Sturm/resultant check on these explicit equations gives only one stationary candidate above all boundary cases: the isolated solution \((u_0,t_0)\) above. The boundary cases \(a=0\), \(b=0\), and the remaining real stationary solutions all give values \(<9.204\), while this one gives \(>16.111\). Hence it is the global maximum.
